known as a “biological response regulator” because of its multiple biological functions [1].
The first defensive line of body immunity is innate immunity. In its early stage, it mainly
uses phagocytic cells such as macrophages and neutrophils to engulf and kill pathogens
invading the body and then further activates the adaptive immune system by secreting
cytokines and chemokines. β-glucan has been found to affect several types of immune
cells, including macrophages, natural killer cells, and neutrophils, resulting in various
immunological effects. In recent decades, tumor immunotherapy has made extensive
use of β-glucan as a natural biological effect regulator [2]. Current clinical applications
